findings.summary: the new method was inserted BETWEEN refusalsSeen()'s javadoc and refusalsSeen(), orphaning it -- javac now warns [dangling-doc-comments] at this line
findings.detail: At HEAD the M5.28 block at line 145 ('Partition refusals the store raised inside a release window ... THIS IS WHAT MAKES refusedForAnotherPod FALSIFIABLE') was attached to `int refusalsSeen()`. The diff inserts a second javadoc (166-192) plus `int releasedDespiteOwnPartition()` (193-195) between them, so the M5.28 block now attaches to nothing and `refusalsSeen()` (197) is undocumented. MEASURED, not inferred: `./gradlew :sequencer:compileTestJava --rerun-tasks` emits `GracefulReleaseMeter.java:145: warning: [dangling-doc-comments] documentation comment is not attached to any declaration`, which is NOT present at HEAD. The other dangling warnings in this module (FaultInjectingStore:261,:415) are deliberate standalone notes; this one is an accidental detachment. Failure scenario: generated javadoc drops the M5.28 block entirely and `refusalsSeen()` ships undocumented, while a reader of the source (or an IDE reader scrolling up from `releasedDespiteOwnPartition()`) sees the refusals-seen prose -- 'REFUSALS, NOT RELEASES, and the unit is load-bearing', 'THIS IS WHAT MAKES refusedForAnotherPod FALSIFIABLE' -- sitting directly above the M5.31 counter and attributes the falsifiability argument and the WINDOWS-vs-REFUSALS unit warning to the wrong counter. That unit warning exists precisely because this file's own history records the claim being re-derived wrongly. Fix is one move: put the new javadoc+method after `refusalsSeen()`, or above it, so each block sits on its own declaration.
findings.failure_scenario: A future hand tightening the `SEEDS / 50` floor (M5.28/M5.30's open thread) opens GracefulReleaseMeter.java, finds `refusalsSeen()` with no javadoc, and reads the detached M5.28 block -- 'REFUSALS, NOT RELEASES, and the unit is load-bearing' and 'THIS IS WHAT MAKES refusedForAnotherPod FALSIFIABLE' -- as documentation of `releasedDespiteOwnPartition()`, the method it now sits directly above. They conclude the M5.31 counter is the one carrying the falsifiability argument and the WINDOWS-vs-REFUSALS unit, which is false of it and is the exact re-derivation that block was written to prevent. In generated javadoc the block is dropped entirely (javac already reports it as attached to no declaration) so the rationale is simply gone.

findings.summary: the counter sees only the wrongly-allowed releases that COMPLETED; one whose write landed through the ambiguousPut arm and then threw is equally wrongly allowed and is invisible, and no comment says so
findings.detail: `releasedDespiteOwnPartition++` sits inside the `completed && putIfMatch moved` branch, so it inherits `released()`'s scope. With M5.26's defect present and the leader partitioned, the stale un-partitioned actor gets the call past `refuseIfPartitioned`, and on the ~3% of conditional writes where `ambiguousPut` fires the write LANDS on the delegate (the lease is written expired for a partitioned leader -- exactly the harm the row describes) and then throws: `completed` is false, nothing is credited and nothing is counted. Same for the withheldPut arm, where nothing lands but the store still ACCEPTED a call it should have refused. Dropping the `completed` conjunct is NOT the fix (M5.29 measured `record` running above `refuseIfPartitioned`, so a refused call already moves the verb counter -- 38 legitimate refusals would become false positives on a correct tree), so the limit looks inherent given where the verb counter sits. The finding is that it is unstated: `released()`'s own javadoc spends three paragraphs on 'ISSUED, NOT WROTE' and 'NOT reached the store', while the new javadoc and the backlog cell say only 'the sweep now REDS on both directions', with no note that the allowed direction is covered for completed releases only. In this workload the gap is unobserved (the single wrongly-allowed window at seed 323 completes), so it is a prose gap today and a measurement gap the first time the ambiguous arm lands on one.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.26's defect returns in a tree where the ambiguousPut arm fires on the release write: the conditional write LANDS (the lease is written expired on behalf of a partitioned leader, which is the harm the row names) and then throws, so `completed` is false, `released` is not credited and `releasedDespiteOwnPartition` stays 0. The sweep's `isZero` passes on a run that contained a wrongly-allowed release, and the backlog cell's claim that 'the sweep now REDS on both directions' is untrue for that run. Today it is latent -- the one wrongly-allowed window over 1,000 seeds (seed 323) completes -- so the immediate cost is a reader trusting a coverage claim wider than the code makes.

findings.summary: the new Result component's wire is unconstrained: passing refusedForAnotherPod() twice at the construction site survives the whole suite and silently reinstates the blindness M5.31 exists to end
findings.detail: `Result` now ends in FOUR adjacent `int` components fed from one object. M5.28's round already measured this class of mis-wire and bought a guard for it (`gracefulReleaseRefusalsSeen < gracefulReleases`, line 464-467 of the sweep). The new component has no equivalent, and nothing outside the sweep reads it -- `GracefulReleaseMeterTest:69` asserts the METER, not the Result. Mutation that survives: replace `releases.releasedDespiteOwnPartition()` with a second `releases.refusedForAnotherPod()`. On a correct tree both are 0 and the suite is green; with M5.26's defect reinstated the sweep still reds, but at the OLD assertion and for the old reason, so the M5.31 counter is dead and the claim 'the sweep REDS on both directions' is false while every gate is green. I can see no assertion that closes this -- unlike M5.28's case there is no numeric relation available, because the honest value is 0 in every scenario this tree can produce -- so this is recorded as the residual rather than as a demand.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone edits the 19-component `Result` construction (a rename, a reorder, a copy-paste of the adjacent line) and passes `releases.refusedForAnotherPod()` where `releases.releasedDespiteOwnPartition()` belongs. Both are 0 on a correct tree, so the sweep, GracefulReleaseMeterTest and the rest of the suite stay green and no gate notices. The M5.31 counter is now dead: when M5.26's defect next returns the sweep reds only at the old assertion, blaming the refusal direction, and the ALLOWED direction is once again a number that moves in the totals and in no assertion -- the precise state this task exists to end.
